contract.question: Parse one bounded exact local CSV byte snapshot and validate its identity, numeric grammar, currency and calendar-label context before holdings valuation.
contract.inputs: UTF-8 local file <=1000000 bytes, exact ordered asset/quantity/price/currency/valuation_date header, 1–10000 correctly sized rows; unique trimmed literal IDs, unsigned ordinary decimal quantities/prices and explicit expected uppercase three-letter currency/calendar date.
contract.outputs: Indexed float64 holdings values, finite scalar total and evidence for the same parsed bytes: SHA256, byte count, row count and expected context.
contract.oracle: Literal IDs00123,BETA,NA;6×100+3×100+1×100=1000. LF fixture SHA256 e68b437d0a8476c1b21a01a0ae4577144b54c79b8383d1f0d9779dd958297c11; CRLF changes bytes/hash while the controlled parsed table stays equal.
contract.limits: Hash is byte identity, not authenticity/freshness. File path and expected context are caller-owned; one bounded read is not an OS transactional snapshot against concurrent writers. No FX, intraday/session/calendar availability or arbitrary file/service integration is established.

contract.outputs: Aligned report in expected weight order, summary expected/observed/missing/absent/complete counts, and either a finite complete scalar total or None. Never fill, drop expected names or renormalize observed weights.
contract.oracle: Complete fixture9/200=0.045. A/C-only fixture has expected3,observed2,missing1,absent1 and totalNone. Explicit missing B has absent0. Empty return source has missing3/absent3. Observed zero permits total0; missing zero-weight asset still blocks the total.
contract.limits: Completeness is relative to caller-supplied expected identities, not vendor/feed authenticity. Partial sums/renormalized observed totals describe another question. Price-only assumptions, common interval/currency and numerical-range/inference limitations remain; no market data repair or financial release approval.

contract.question: Normalize only explicitly permitted formatting, validate all records, quarantine all normalized duplicate keys and retain a full source-row audit.
contract.inputs: Exact ordered asset/quantity/price/currency text schema,1–10000 rows,cells strings<=64 chars; same valuation instant/common USD long-only contract. Strip fields, uppercase currency only; asset case significant. Duplicate original row index allowed because source_row is a new local ordinal.
contract.outputs: Accepted numeric holdings table, rejected raw records with normalized asset/reasons, and one changed/status/reason audit row per local source ordinal. No batch aggregate is returned; any rejection means the fixture batch is not valuation-ready.
contract.oracle: Six rows conserve as2 accepted(ALPHA,CASH) and4 rejected; values600/100. Both BETA rows quarantined, including the raw spaced token. Two rows changed under normalization. Bad numeric and EUR rows retain explicit reasons.
contract.limits: Normalization is specific to this source policy, unlike strict whitespace rejection in7.5/7.6; currency spelling normalization is not FX. Accepted subtotal700 is not a complete batch valuation. Local ordinals are not global identity, read-only enforcement is absent, and provenance/concurrency/extreme monetary accuracy remain broader integration limits.
